concepts.label: CS Subfields and Their Big Questions

study_sequence.directive: Define data vs. information and summarize why representation (encoding, structure, and meaning) matters for computation. Give examples of representing the same information in different forms and the tradeoffs those forms impose on processing.

Explain what computation is and how algorithms specify computational steps that can be executed by a machine. Provide at least one example of an algorithmic solution to a problem and identify the inputs, outputs, and step-by-step procedure.

Describe abstraction as the practice of hiding detail to manage complexity and building models that capture what matters for a task. Show how the same real-world problem can be represented at different abstraction levels and why that affects solution design.

Characterize the major components of a computer system (hardware, operating system, applications) and how they cooperate to execute programs. Outline how system design choices (e.g., memory, processing, I/O) constrain or enable algorithms.

Explain how programs realize algorithms using programming languages and how software is developed, tested, and maintained. Distinguish at a high level between source code, compilation/interpretation, and execution.

Identify the major subfields of computer science and state the kinds of questions/problems each subfield addresses. Map example real-world problems to the subfields that would most directly contribute solutions.
